source.title: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
source.authors: Tom McGrath; Matthew Rahtz; János Kramár; Vladimir Mikulik; S. Legg

page_placements.theme: Repair and redundancy extend beyond IOI name movers

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests the related self-repair behavior with layer-level resample ablations and logit-effect measures, rather than testing the GPT-2 small IOI circuit itself.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on compensation after ablations, which bear on backup behavior. It does not test IOI prompts, the 26-head circuit, or its head classes. The cited GPT-2 Small backup-head result is prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures layer-level self-repair (the 'Hydra effect') in Chinchilla 7B on Counterfact factual-recall prompts. It does not run IOI prompts, use GPT-2 small, or ablate name-mover or any individual heads. V2 names backup name-mover heads inside the GPT-2 small IOI circuit, so these results are a related but different construct, not a test of V2. The authors only discuss the link, saying their findings corroborate the backup-heads result and contradict the original paper's dropout explanation. None of the other versions are touched.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that, because Chinchilla 7B was trained without dropout, they disprove the original IOI paper's hypothesis that dropout causes backup behaviour. They also note that the analysis is layer-level only, and they leave head-level replication as future work.
record.recipe_differences: This study uses layer-level resample ablations in Chinchilla 7B and measures logit effects on Counterfact factual-recall prompts; it does not test GPT-2 small IOI head ablations.
record.method_sensitivity: Compensation varies with network depth and the ablated layer; the balance between attention compensation and MLP response shifts with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: In Chinchilla 7B, trained without dropout, ablating an attention layer makes a downstream attention layer raise its direct effect (Hydra effect), while late MLP erasure falls. Together these restore about 70% of the logit reduction at middle layers, and compensation explains 92% of ΔDE variance at layer 23. Compensation is incomplete: the slope is below one past layer 13.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-repair/backup behaviour after ablation occurs at the layer level in other LLMs and tasks (factual recall), including models trained without dropout, and it compensates only partially.

record.problems: The evidence is from one model and factual-recall prompts, not IOI. The analysis is at layer rather than individual-head granularity. Some examples are illustrative, and much of the layer-by-layer evidence is presented in figures.

untested.parts: All: the GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
All as stated: ablating name-mover heads in GPT-2 small IOI and takeover by backup heads. The study's self-repair is layer-level, in Chinchilla 7B, on factual recall.
All: IOI circuits with the same head classes in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse of their components.
All: whether other discovery methods, ablations or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
All: evaluation sensitivity of the IOI circuit's faithfulness and completeness.
All: IOI across name orders, templates and numbers of names.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V2 labels overreaches. The study never touches IOI or GPT-2 small, and the V2 link rests only on the authors' discussion. The claim that dropout does not cause self-repair is relevant context for V2, but V2 as stated says nothing about cause. A future claim version on self-repair beyond IOI could take these rows.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 attention heads and 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality.
The study does not ablate individual name-mover heads or test the IOI task; it measures compensation after layer ablations in Chinchilla 7B.
Whether IOI circuits with the same head classes and roles occur across models, sizes, checkpoints, or other tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
Evaluation sensitivity and circuit completeness for the IOI circuit.
IOI behavior across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

rows.subject: Chinchilla 7B
rows.operation_detail: Resample-ablated an attention layer and measured compensatory direct effects in downstream layers.
rows.measure: Variance in downstream direct-effect changes explained by compensation
rows.note: The authors identify layer 23 as the high point of this effect; the variance explained is not a measure of complete behavioral restoration.
rows.check: Layer-level compensation in Chinchilla 7B on factual recall, not name-mover backup in the IOI circuit. The 92% is variance in downstream ΔDE explained by compensation at layer 23; it is not a restoration fraction.

rows.subject: Chinchilla 7B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated layers and measured the combined compensatory response of downstream attention and MLP layers.
rows.measure: Fraction of the reduction in token logits restored by the Hydra effect and MLP responses
rows.note: The authors report approximate restoration, not full restoration.
rows.check: About 70% logit restoration is summed attention (Hydra) plus reduced MLP erasure at middle layers, in a non-IOI setting. It is not head-level backup within the IOI circuit.

rows.subject: Chinchilla 7B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated layers and compared downstream compensatory effects with direct effects.
rows.measure: Slope of linear regression between direct effect and compensatory response
rows.value: less than one at all layers past layer 13
rows.note: The authors say this implies a nonzero total effect after ablation.
rows.check: A regression slope below one past layer 13 means compensation is incomplete. The setting is not IOI and the granularity is layers, not heads.

rows.subject: Chinchilla 7B
rows.operation_detail: Resample-ablated attention layer 18 and observed the effect on subsequent attention layers.
rows.measure: Change in downstream attention-layer impact on the maximum-likelihood logit
rows.value: Layer 20 substantially increases its impact and partially compensates
rows.note: The paper presents this as an illustrative example, not a dataset-wide estimate.
rows.check: A single illustrative prompt (layer 18 ablated, layer 20 compensates), not a dataset estimate, in a non-IOI setting.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 1 caption identifies attention layer 18 ablation; Section 2.5.2 identifies layer 20 compensation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Figure 1 caption identifies attention layer 18 ablation; Section 2.5.2 identifies layer 20 compensation.

relation.reason: The introduction and conclusion explicitly connect the Hydra effect to the IOI paper's backup heads, without testing or using that circuit.

tranche.reason: Layer-level self-repair during factual recall does not test any listed IOI claim version. The study does not identify IOI head classes or test the GPT-2 small circuit.

source_check.notes: The 92% measures explained variance, whereas approximately 70% describes combined logit restoration. The authors argue that dropout is unnecessary for self-repair; individual attention-head analysis remains future work.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Chinchilla 7B factual-recall prompts after layer ablations
reader_labels.reason: Downstream compensation is reported after ablation, including a substantial response at layer 23 and the illustrative layer-18 ablation (R1, R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Middle layers and layers past layer 13 in Chinchilla 7B
reader_labels.reason: Compensation is incomplete: the reported restoration is approximately 70%, and the regression slope remains below one (R2, R3). The study does not establish takeover by IOI name-mover backup heads.
